papers.title: Effect of Powder Reuse on the Corrosion Behavior of Anodized and Flash-Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation-Treated Laser-Powder Bed Fusion Ti-6Al-4V ELI
papers.abstract: The present work compares the corrosion performance of additively manufactured (AM) Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Extra-Low Interstitials) alloy manufactured by Laser-Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) using virgin powder (Cycle 1/C1 sample) and reused powder feedstock after up to 34 cycles (Cycle 34/C34 sample) of manufacturing. The effect of powder reuse is also evaluated for anodizing and Flash-PEO-coated specimens in Harrison’s (25 °C) and Hanks’ solutions (37 °C), representing simulated atmospheric precipitation and physiological conditions, respectively. Specimens were characterized using common metallographic techniques, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy and optical profilometry. Corrosion resistance was evaluated using cyclic potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) tests. The oxygen content in the Ti-6Al-4V reaches 0.14 wt.% after 34 cycles (C34) of powder reuse, enhancing its passivity in both Harrison’s and Hanks’ solutions. Both virgin and reused powder builds are susceptible to localized corrosion in Hanks’ solution at potentials above 1.75 V. Melt pool borders are thought to be the preferential sites for localized corrosion, as indicated by Volta potential measurements (ΔV = 100 mV). The number of cycles does not significantly affect the current–voltage responses for anodizing and flash-Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation (Flash-PEO) treatments, although anodizing is slightly more responsive to variations in surface roughness (i.e., real specimen area). Anodizing and Flash-PEO reduce the passive current density by nearly two orders of magnitude. Even after surface treatment, the alloy printed with reused powder revealed better passivity. Flash-PEO coatings yielded significant protection against localized corrosion. This unlocks Flash-PEO processing as a successful protection approach for AM biomedical components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了后处理（阳极氧化和Flash-PEO）对Ti-6Al-4V腐蚀行为的影响，未涉及机械性能（如疲劳、拉伸），与方向关注点偏离。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not investigate mechanical performance (fatigue, tensile strength, or porosity closure) of Ti-6Al-4V after post-processing; it focuses solely on corrosion behavior in simulated physiological and atmospheric solutions.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究粉末复用和后处理（阳极氧化、Flash-PEO）对LPBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI腐蚀性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 采用循环动电位极化测试，结合XRD、SEM等表征腐蚀行为
summary_zh.result: 粉末复用34周期后氧含量增至0.14wt%，增强钝化；Flash-PEO显著提升局部腐蚀抗力
summary_zh.validation: 通过对比不同粉末状态和表面处理的极化曲线验证

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates how powder reuse up to 34 cycles affects the corrosion resistance of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI after anodizing and flash-PEO surface treatments.
summary_en.method: Cyclic potentiodynamic polarization tests, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and optical profilometry were employed to characterize corrosion behavior and surface morphology.
summary_en.result: Reused powder (34 cycles) increased oxygen content to 0.14 wt.%, enhancing passivity; flash-PEO coatings provided superior protection against localized corrosion, reducing passive current density by nearly two orders of magnitude.
summary_en.validation: Corrosion resistance was validated through polarization curves in Harrison's and Hanks' solutions, comparing virgin and reused powder builds with different surface treatments.

papers.title: Unveiling heterogeneous microstructure and deformation behavior in laser-directed energy deposition repaired wrought Ti-6Al-4V thin walls

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接涉及激光定向能量沉积修复的Ti-6Al-4V薄壁的微观结构和变形行为，属于L1方向的力学性能研究。
llm.why_not_core: Does not report fatigue life or S-N curves; focuses on static deformation and microstructure heterogeneity rather than cyclic fatigue performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示激光定向能量沉积修复Ti-6Al-4V薄壁的异质微观结构和变形机制。
summary_zh.method: 采用激光定向能量沉积技术修复锻造Ti-6Al-4V薄壁，并进行微观结构表征和力学测试。
summary_zh.result: 发现了修复区域的异质微观结构及其对整体变形行为的影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观结构观察和力学性能测试验证了结果。

summary_en.motivation: To uncover the heterogeneous microstructure and deformation behavior in laser-directed energy deposition repaired wrought Ti-6Al-4V thin walls.
summary_en.method: Laser-directed energy deposition was used to repair wrought Ti-6Al-4V thin walls, followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Heterogeneous microstructures were observed in the repaired region, influencing the overall deformation behavior.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation was performed through microstructural analysis and mechanical property measurements.
